content.name: ASRS v1.1
content.summary: 18-item adult ADHD screener with Part A (6 items) and Part B (12 items).
content.description: The ASRS v1.1 is a validated screening tool for adult ADHD aligned with DSM criteria. Part A (items 1-6) is the primary screener, while Part B (items 7-18) provides additional symptom context.
content.purpose: Screen for adult ADHD and assess symptom patterns across inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity domains.

items.text: How often do you have trouble wrapping up the final details of a project, once the challenging parts have been done?
How often do you have difficulty getting things in order when you have to do a task that requires organization?
How often do you have problems remembering appointments or obligations?
When you have a task that requires a lot of thought, how often do you avoid or delay getting started?
How often do you fidget or squirm with your hands or feet when you have to sit down for a long time?
How often do you feel overly active and compelled to do things, like you were driven by a motor?
How often do you make careless mistakes when you have to work on a boring or difficult project?
How often do you have difficulty keeping your attention when you are doing boring or repetitive work?
How often do you have difficulty concentrating on what people say to you, even when they are speaking to you directly?
How often do you misplace or have difficulty finding things at home or at work?
How often are you distracted by activity or noise around you?
How often do you leave your seat in meetings or other situations in which you are expected to remain seated?
How often do you feel restless or fidgety?
How often do you have difficulty unwinding and relaxing when you have time to yourself?
How often do you find yourself talking too much when you are in social situations?
When you're in a conversation, how often do you find yourself finishing the sentences of the people you are talking to, before they can finish them themselves?
How often do you have difficulty waiting your turn in situations when turn taking is required?
How often do you interrupt others when they are busy?

clinical_interpretations.Low: Your scores indicate minimal ADHD symptoms. Part A score ≤9 and total score ≤30 are both below clinical thresholds, consistent with typical adult functioning without clinically significant ADHD symptoms.
clinical_interpretations.Mild to Moderate: Your scores are in the mild to moderate range. If Part A is 10-13 (below diagnostic threshold) but total score approaches 40+ (79th percentile), clinical evaluation may still be warranted as this pattern can be diagnostically informative.
clinical_interpretations.High: Your scores indicate clinically significant ADHD symptoms. Part A scores 14-17 meet the diagnostic threshold, and/or total scores 40-49 exceed the 79th percentile where most individuals with ADHD score. Professional evaluation is recommended.
clinical_interpretations.Very High: Your scores indicate severe ADHD symptoms. Part A scores ≥18 or total scores ≥50 represent very high symptom levels that are strongly consistent with ADHD diagnosis and require comprehensive clinical evaluation.

sections.title: About the ASRS v1.1
sections.text: The Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS) v1.1 is a validated screening tool based on DSM criteria. Part A (items 1-6) is the most predictive for ADHD screening, while Part B (items 7-18) provides additional symptom severity information across inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity domains.

sections.title: Instructions
sections.text: For each item, choose how often the problem has occurred over the past 6 months. Please answer each question as honestly as possible based on your recent experiences.

sections.title: Scoring and Interpretation
sections.text: Part A scores of 14 or higher suggest symptoms consistent with ADHD and warrant professional evaluation. The assessment provides scores for overall symptom severity and specific symptom domains including inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity.

psychometric_properties.validation: Validated against DSM-IV and DSM-5 ADHD criteria

clinical_alerts.adhd_screening: Part A scores ≥14 indicate positive ADHD screening and recommend professional evaluation

clinical_interpretations.Low Risk: You are at low risk of health and other problems from your current pattern of use. Brief advice about lower-risk use and routine monitoring during health visits is appropriate.
clinical_interpretations.Moderate Risk: You are at risk of health and other problems from your current pattern of substance use. Brief intervention including structured advice, self-help materials, and follow-up within 1-3 months is recommended. Specialist referral may be considered if brief intervention is unsuccessful or multiple substances are involved.
clinical_interpretations.High Risk: You are at high risk of experiencing severe problems (health, social, financial, legal, relationship) as a result of your current pattern of use and are likely to be dependent. Further assessment and more intensive treatment including specialist drug and alcohol treatment services is recommended.
clinical_interpretations.Injection Drug Use: History of injection drug use significantly increases health risks including blood-borne viruses (HIV, Hepatitis B/C), collapsed veins, abscesses, and overdose. Immediate specialist referral for comprehensive assessment, harm reduction strategies, and treatment planning is strongly recommended.

sections.title: About the ASSIST v3.0
sections.text: The WHO Alcohol, Smoking and Substance Involvement Screening Test (ASSIST) v3.0 is a validated screening instrument that identifies substance use risk across 10 categories. It provides specific risk levels and intervention recommendations based on standardized WHO criteria and has been validated in multiple countries and healthcare settings.

sections.title: Instructions
sections.text: Please answer each question honestly based on your substance use experiences. For prescription medications, only consider non-medical use (taking more than prescribed, using without a prescription, or using for non-medical reasons). All responses are confidential and will help determine appropriate next steps for your health and wellbeing.

sections.title: Scoring and Interpretation
sections.text: The ASSIST calculates separate involvement scores for each substance category by adding scores from questions 2-7 (excluding tobacco question 5). Risk levels are determined by specific thresholds: tobacco and illicit substances use 0-3/4-26/27+ thresholds, while alcohol uses 0-10/11-26/27+ thresholds reflecting its legal status and different risk profile.

content.name: GAD-7
content.summary: A 7-item anxiety screening tool with scoring guidelines.
content.description: A 7-question instrument for screening, diagnosing, monitoring and measuring the severity of generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). The GAD-7 is widely used in healthcare and research settings worldwide.
content.purpose: Screen for generalized anxiety disorder and monitor treatment response

items.text: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
Not being able to stop or control worrying
Worrying too much about different things
Trouble relaxing
Being so restless that it is hard to sit still
Becoming easily annoyed or irritable
Feeling afraid as if something awful might happen

severe_anxiety.message: Severe anxiety - may require clinical intervention

clinical_interpretations.Minimal: Your score suggests minimal anxiety symptoms. This is within the normal range. Continue monitoring your mental health and maintain healthy coping strategies such as regular exercise, adequate sleep, and stress management techniques.
clinical_interpretations.Mild: Your score indicates mild anxiety symptoms that may occasionally interfere with daily activities. Consider lifestyle modifications including regular physical activity, mindfulness practices, limiting caffeine intake, and ensuring adequate sleep. If symptoms persist or worsen over several weeks, consider consulting a healthcare professional.
clinical_interpretations.Moderate: Your score suggests moderate anxiety symptoms that are likely interfering with your daily activities and quality of life. It is recommended to consult with a healthcare professional for proper evaluation. Treatment options may include counseling, therapy (such as cognitive-behavioral therapy), lifestyle modifications, or other evidence-based interventions.
clinical_interpretations.Severe: Your score indicates severe anxiety symptoms that are significantly impacting your daily functioning and well-being. It is important to consult with a healthcare professional promptly for comprehensive evaluation and treatment planning. Severe anxiety is highly treatable with appropriate professional care, which may include therapy, medication, or a combination of treatments.

sections.title: About the GAD-7
sections.text: The Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) is a brief self-report tool designed to screen for generalized anxiety disorder and assess its severity. It is based on DSM-IV criteria for GAD and is also useful for identifying other anxiety disorders.

sections.title: Instructions
sections.text: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following problems? For each item, select the response that best describes your experience.

sections.title: Scoring and Interpretation
sections.text: Add up all checked boxes for a total score. Anxiety severity bands: 0–4 minimal, 5–9 mild, 10–14 moderate, 15–21 severe anxiety.

sections.title: Clinical Applications
sections.text: The GAD-7 is widely used in primary care, mental health, and research settings. It can be used for initial screening, monitoring treatment progress, and assessing outcomes for anxiety disorders.

clinical_alerts.severe_anxiety: Scores ≥15 indicate severe anxiety and may require clinical intervention

content.name: PHQ-9
content.summary: A 9-item depression screening tool with scoring guidelines.
content.description: A 9-question instrument for screening, diagnosing, monitoring and measuring the severity of depression.

items.text: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless
Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
Feeling tired or having little energy
Poor appetite or overeating
Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed. Or the opposite — being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself

suicide_risk.message: Suicide risk screen positive - requires immediate clinical attention

clinical_interpretations.Minimal: Your score indicates minimal depression symptoms. This suggests you are experiencing few if any depressive symptoms that interfere with your daily life. Continue with healthy lifestyle practices including regular exercise, adequate sleep, social connections, and stress management techniques.
clinical_interpretations.Mild: Your score suggests mild depression symptoms that may occasionally affect your daily activities. Consider implementing self-care strategies such as regular physical activity, maintaining social connections, practicing stress reduction techniques, and ensuring adequate sleep. If symptoms persist for more than two weeks or worsen, consider consulting with a healthcare professional.
clinical_interpretations.Moderate: Your score indicates moderate depression that is likely impacting your daily functioning and quality of life. It is recommended to consult with a healthcare professional for proper evaluation and discussion of treatment options. Effective treatments may include counseling, psychotherapy (such as cognitive-behavioral therapy), lifestyle modifications, and in some cases, medication.
clinical_interpretations.Moderately severe: Your score suggests moderately severe depression that is significantly affecting your daily life and well-being. Professional evaluation and treatment are strongly recommended. Depression at this level typically responds well to treatment, which may include psychotherapy, medication, or a combination of both, along with lifestyle support strategies.
clinical_interpretations.Severe: Your score indicates severe depression that is substantially impairing your ability to function in daily activities. Immediate consultation with a healthcare professional is strongly recommended for comprehensive evaluation and treatment planning. Severe depression is highly treatable with appropriate professional care, and early intervention can significantly improve outcomes and quality of life.

sections.title: About DBSA
sections.text: The Depression and Bipolar Support Alliance (DBSA) is the leading peer-directed national organization focusing on depression and bipolar disorder. DBSA provides hope, help, support, and education to improve the lives of people who have mood disorders.

sections.title: Support Groups
sections.text: DBSA offers hundreds of peer-led support groups across the United States and online. These groups provide a safe, confidential environment where people can share experiences, coping skills, and information. Support groups are free and open to anyone living with depression or bipolar disorder, as well as their family and friends.

sections.title: How to Find a Group
sections.text: Visit dbsalliance.org and use the chapter locator to find in-person groups near you, or join online groups through their website. No registration or diagnosis required - all are welcome.
